note: Source: cursor c is derived from the untrusted heap input buffer in_buf (fuzzer data of size in_size); c walks the logfmt bytes.
Key scan advances c past the key 'a' until c points at '='; here the bounds check correctly precedes the ident_byte lookup.
c points at '='; c++ moves c to the first value byte, the single trailing digit '1' (the last byte of the 3-byte input).
Guard confirms c is still in bounds before the unquoted-value parse begins; it is, because c points at the final digit.
Root cause: the digit-scan loop tests ident_byte[*c] BEFORE (c < end). After consuming the single digit, c++ makes c == end and the condition re-dereferences *c one byte past the heap buffer.
Sink: ident_byte is indexed with *c while c == end (in_buf + in_size), a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow READ reported by ASAN.
